title: Gold Demand Trends: India Focus Q2 2026
gist: Indian gold demand fell to 131t in Q2 2026 (-6% y/y, -13% q/q) yet spending hit a quarterly record of INR1,979bn (US$21bn) as domestic MCX prices stayed 59% higher y/y, propped up by a mid-May 9% import duty hike and a 4% q/q rupee depreciation. Jewellery volumes made their second-weakest Q2 since 2000 while India still led the world at 27% of global jewellery demand; supply collapsed to a six-year low of 120t on 98t of net bullion imports, and gold-backed retail lending exploded to INR5.1tn at banks (+105% y/y) as holders monetised rather than sold gold.

themes.theme: Q2 2026 India headline demand and price levels

insights.claim: Indian gold demand softened to 131t in Q2 2026, down 6% y/y and 13% q/q, leaving volumes well below the quarter's long-term average of 188t.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Volume weakness at record prices confirms Indian physical demand is now the marginal price-taker, not a price-setter — watch tonnage, not value, for genuine demand strength.
insights.quote: India's gold demand softened to 131t in Q2, down 6% y/y and 13% q/q, with volumes remaining below the quarter's long-term average of 188t.
insights.locator: A measured quarter: demand and price

insights.claim: Indian spending on gold reached a quarterly record of INR1,979bn (US$21bn) in Q2 2026, up 50% y/y in rupee terms and 35% y/y in US dollar terms, even as tonnage fell.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Record rupee spend on falling tonnage means jeweller revenue can grow while volumes shrink — bullish for retail margins, ambiguous for physical offtake.
insights.quote: Yet with prices at elevated levels, spending on gold was at a quarterly record of INR1,979bn (US$21bn)
insights.locator: A measured quarter: demand and price

insights.claim: The average LBMA Gold Price PM fell 7.5% q/q to US$4,506 in Q2 2026 but remained 37.4% higher y/y, marking a pause after the exceptional rally through 2024, 2025 and early 2026.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A single-digit quarterly drawdown after a multi-year run is the kind of consolidation that historically re-triggers Indian dip-buying rather than ending the trend.
insights.locator: After an exceptional rally through 2024, 2025

insights.claim: The domestic MCX spot gold price was broadly flat q/q at INR1,50,733 per 10g in Q2 2026 and 58.9% higher y/y, insulated from the international decline by the mid-May import duty hike and a 4% q/q rupee depreciation.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Indian buyers got no relief from the dollar gold pullback — duty plus FX is a structural wedge that keeps domestic affordability stressed even in global corrections.
insights.quote: the domestic MCX spot gold price was broadly flat, supported by the import duty hike and the rupee depreciation (down by 4% q/q)
insights.locator: After an exceptional rally through 2024, 2025

insights.claim: H1 2026 Indian gold demand totalled 281.5t, up just 1.8% y/y, while H1 value surged 72.5% y/y to INR4,254.2bn (US$45.8bn).
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Flat half-year tonnage against a 72% value jump quantifies how much of India's 'demand growth' is pure price, not incremental metal.
insights.locator: Table 1: India gold demand by sector

themes.theme: Jewellery: volumes squeezed, value at records

insights.claim: Indian jewellery demand was 75t in Q2 2026, rebounding 14% q/q from a weak Q1 but down 15% y/y — the second-lowest Q2 in the World Gold Council's quarterly series going back to 2000.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A near-record-low Q2 in 26 years of data sets the volume floor investors should benchmark any festive-season recovery against.
insights.quote: At 75t, it rebounded 14% q/q from a weak Q1 but remained 15% lower y/y — making it the second-lowest Q2 in our quarterly data series going back to 2000.
insights.locator: Jewellery spending outweighs lower volumes

insights.claim: The value of Indian jewellery demand rose 34% y/y and 13% q/q to INR1,132bn (US$12bn) in Q2 2026 despite the 15% y/y volume decline.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Listed Indian jewellery retailers can post strong revenue growth on shrinking tonnage — screen for volume/mix disclosure, not headline sales.
insights.quote: the value of jewellery demand rose 34% y/y and 13% q/q to INR1,132bn/US$12bn
insights.locator: But lower volumes did not translate

insights.claim: Q2 2026 Indian jewellery buying started strong on Akshaya Tritiya and wedding demand as prices eased from Q1 peaks, then weakened from mid-quarter due to the month-long inauspicious period (mid-May to mid-June), the 9% import duty hike, and the Prime Minister's appeal to curb gold purchases.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Political jawboning against gold buying is a new, non-price demand risk in India that can appear without warning ahead of import data.
insights.quote: Demand weakened from mid-quarter as the month-long inauspicious period (mid-May to mid-June), the 9% import duty hike, and the Prime Minister's appeal to curb gold purchases weighed on demand.
insights.locator: The quarter began strongly, supported by Akshaya Tritiya

insights.claim: The nearly 60% y/y rise in Indian gold prices is accelerating a structural mix shift toward lighter-weight, lower-carat and studded jewellery as affordability is constrained.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Grammage-per-piece is falling faster than piece counts — a durable headwind to gold tonnage that flatters retailers' studded-jewellery margins.
insights.quote: accelerating the shift towards lighter-weight, lower-carat and studded jewellery
insights.locator: The nearly 60% y/y rise in gold prices

insights.claim: Indian retailers reported a 10%–20% increase in old-gold exchange volumes in Q2 2026, with exchange-led purchases accounting for up to 70% of sales in some cases.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Up to 70% exchange-funded sales means headline retail demand is increasingly gold-for-gold churn, not fresh metal absorption from imports.
insights.quote: Retailers reported a 10%–20% increase in exchange volumes, with such purchases accounting for up to 70% of sales in some cases.
insights.locator: Exchange-led purchases gained further traction

insights.claim: India was the world's largest gold jewellery market in Q2 2026, accounting for 27% of global demand, with a smaller y/y decline (-15%) than China (-28%), the United States (-25%), the UAE (-28%) or Iran (-26%).
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: India is the least-bad consumer market at these prices; relative resilience makes it the key swing region for any global jewellery recovery trade.
insights.quote: India was the world's largest gold jewellery market in the quarter, accounting for 27% of global demand
insights.locator: India was the world's largest gold jewellery market

insights.claim: Continued store expansion and stocking kept Indian jeweller inventories elevated at around 21t in Q2 2026, well above the 13-year average of 15t.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A 6t inventory overhang above trend cushions supply but can also suppress near-term import demand if festive sell-through disappoints.
insights.locator: Continued store expansion and related stocking

insights.claim: Early signs point to an uptick in Indian jewellery demand from late June 2026 on lower and relatively stable prices, with retailers building inventories ahead of a festive season that begins in late August.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Late-August festive restocking is the near-term catalyst for Indian import volumes — monitor July/August customs data for confirmation.
insights.quote: Retailers are reportedly building inventories ahead of the festive season, which begins in late August.
insights.locator: Early signs point to an uptick in jewellery demand

themes.theme: Investment demand and the price-momentum link

insights.claim: Indian investment demand (bars, coins and ETFs) softened to 54t in Q2 2026 from an average of 100t over the preceding three quarters, but stayed modestly above the long-term quarterly average of 49t since 2000.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The floor under Indian investment demand is now above the 25-year norm even after a near-halving — a structurally higher base than pre-2024.
insights.locator: Investment demand tempered by price pause

insights.claim: The World Gold Council attributes the Q2 2026 slowdown in Indian investment demand directly to the pause in the gold price rally, noting rising prices fuelled buying through 2025 and Q1'26 while the Q2 pullback tempered fresh buying.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Indian retail investment is momentum-following, not contrarian — it amplifies rallies and fades corrections, so treat it as a trend confirmer rather than a stabiliser.
insights.quote: This highlights the influence of price momentum on investment behaviour.
insights.locator: The slowdown coincided with a pause in the gold price rally

insights.claim: Indian bar and coin demand fell 19% q/q to 50t in Q2 2026 but was still up 9% y/y, and India accounted for 16% of global bar and coin demand during the quarter with a less pronounced pullback than most other regions.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: India's 16% share and shallower sequential drop makes it the most reliable physical investment bid globally when prices stall.
insights.locator: Bar and coin demand fell 19% q/q to 50t

insights.claim: H1 2026 Indian bar and coin demand reached 113t, the highest in 13 years and well above the 25-year H1 average of 85t.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A 13-year high in physical investment despite record prices signals a regime shift in Indian household allocation toward gold as a savings asset.
insights.quote: H1'26 demand reached 113t, the highest in 13 years and well above the 25-year H1 average of 85t.
insights.locator: Underlying investor interest remained firm

insights.claim: Indian digital gold purchases were estimated at 4.8t in Q2 2026, down from 6.5t in Q1, moderating in April and May before partially recovering in June.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Digital gold is now a measurable ~5t/quarter channel in India — a fast-cycling proxy for retail sentiment ahead of slower physical data.
insights.locator: Digital gold demand also moderated in April and May

insights.claim: India's demand mix rebalanced sharply in Q2 2026, with investment demand falling to 48% of total demand from nearly 70% in Q1, while net jewellery demand accounted for 50%.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A 22-point swing in one quarter shows India's demand composition is now highly unstable — mix, not just level, drives import and price sensitivity.
insights.quote: investment demand accounting for 48% of total demand, down from nearly 70% in Q1
insights.locator: The demand mix rebalanced in Q2

themes.theme: Indian gold ETFs: record H1 despite Q2 cooling

insights.claim: Indian gold ETF demand moderated to 4t in Q2 2026, more than 80% below the record 20t in Q1 and the lowest since Q2'25.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The ETF channel is the most volatile part of Indian demand — an 80%+ swing in one quarter makes it the fastest-moving indicator of domestic sentiment.
insights.locator: Gold ETF demand moderated to 4t in Q2

insights.claim: India, alongside the UK and Hong Kong, was among the few major markets to record positive gold ETF demand in Q2 2026, while the US saw net outflows of 44t and China 22t.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Indian ETF flows decoupled from a heavy Western liquidation cycle — a diversifying flow source worth tracking against US ETF holdings data.
insights.quote: India, alongside the UK and Hong Kong, was among the few major markets to record positive demand, while other markets — in particular the US (-44t) and China (-22t) — saw sizeable net outflows.
insights.locator: Despite the decline, India, alongside the UK

insights.claim: Indian gold ETFs recorded their first monthly net outflow since April 2025 in May 2026, reflecting profit-taking after the 9% import duty hike lifted domestic gold and ETF prices, but investors returned from early June to buy the dips.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Indian ETF holders reliably buy dips within weeks — outflow spikes there have been short-lived and are not a reliable sell signal.
insights.quote: But the outflows were short-lived: investors returned from early June to buy into the price dips, even as global outflows continued.
insights.locator: Flows into Indian gold ETFs were positive in April

insights.claim: H1 2026 Indian gold ETF demand hit a record 24t, up 163% y/y, with total holdings rising to 119t by end-Q2 and AUM up 163% y/y to INR1.7tn (~US$17.6bn).
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A 119t domestic ETF pool with tripling AUM is becoming a material, sticky Indian bid alongside physical demand.
insights.quote: total holdings rose to 119t by end Q2, while AUM increased 163% y/y to INR1.7tn (~US$17.6bn)
insights.locator: Despite the Q2 slowdown, H1'26 ETF demand

themes.theme: Supply squeeze: six-year-low imports and muted recycling

insights.claim: India's total gold supply fell to 120t in Q2 2026, its lowest level in six years and far below the 16-year average of 234t.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Supply running at roughly half its 16-year average is a meaningful drag on India's contribution to the global trade balance and a tell for import-duty-driven distortion.
insights.locator: Lower supply, adequate availability

insights.claim: Indian net bullion imports declined to 98t in Q2 2026, down 22% y/y and 53% q/q, holding up in April on Akshaya Tritiya demand before slowing in May and June as the higher import duty took effect.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A 53% q/q import collapse directly narrows India's gold trade deficit and reduces a chronic source of rupee pressure — relevant to INR positioning.
insights.locator: Net bullion imports, which dominate the supply mix

insights.claim: India's Q2 2026 supply mix was 82% imports, 16% recycling and 2% domestic mine production, with elevated industry inventories and recycled gold keeping availability adequate despite the drop.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: India remains ~82% import-dependent, so any further duty or FX shock passes almost fully into domestic prices.
insights.quote: In Q2 recycling accounted for 16% of supply; domestic mine production for 2%, and imports for 82%.
insights.locator: Despite the decline, supply remained adequate

insights.claim: Net Indian gold recycling fell to 19t in Q2 2026, down 38% q/q and 17% y/y — the lowest level in eleven quarters — even though domestic prices were around 60% higher y/y.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Holders refusing to sell into a 60% price rise removes the classic supply-side brake on rallies; recycling is the single best India indicator of a genuine top.
insights.quote: Despite domestic gold prices being around 60% higher y/y, holders showed limited appetite to sell, preferring to monetise their gold holdings rather than liquidate them.
insights.locator: Net recycling (gold sold for cash) remained subdued

insights.claim: The World Gold Council explicitly reads India's muted recycled supply at 60%-higher prices as pointing to a bullish price outlook for gold.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: This is the report's clearest directional call — a stated bullish signal derived from behaviour rather than forecast, usable as a confirmation input for long-gold positioning.
insights.quote: This has kept recycled supply muted and points to a bullish price outlook for gold.
insights.locator: Net recycling (gold sold for cash) remained subdued

insights.claim: The World Gold Council attributes India's lower Q2 2026 supply to softer demand and reduced import requirements rather than any shortage of gold in the domestic market.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Don't read the six-year-low supply print as physical tightness — it is demand-led, so local premiums are unlikely to spike on it alone.
insights.quote: lower supply reflected softer demand and resultant lower import requirements rather than a shortage of gold in the domestic market
insights.locator: Overall, lower supply reflected softer demand

themes.theme: RBI reserves and the gold-loan credit boom

insights.claim: The RBI's gold holdings have remained steady at 880t since mid-2025, but gold's share of total reserves rose from 12% to 16% purely on the 70% rise in gold prices; RBI purchases were just 0.2t in Q2 2026.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: India's central bank is passively re-weighted into gold without buying — the reserve-share optics may cap further official demand from this buyer.
insights.quote: Although the RBI's gold holdings have remained steady at 880t since mid-2025, gold's share of total reserves has risen from 12% to 16%
insights.locator: RBI maintains stable gold reserves

insights.claim: Outstanding Indian retail gold loans stood at INR5.1tn (US$54bn) for banks, up 105% y/y, and INR3.3tn (US$34.5bn) for NBFCs, up 70% y/y, as of end-May 2026.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A doubling of bank gold-loan books in a year is a direct earnings driver for Indian gold-loan NBFCs and lenders — and a new gold-price-linked credit exposure.
insights.quote: as of end-May, outstanding gold loans stood at INR5.1tn (US$54bn) for banks, up 105% y/y, and INR3.3tn (US$34.5bn) for NBFCs, up 70% y/y
insights.locator: Collateralised borrowing against gold jewellery

insights.claim: Gold loans are now India's second-largest retail lending segment after housing, as borrowers seek liquidity while retaining ownership of their gold.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold-collateralised credit has become systemically relevant in Indian retail lending — a structural growth channel and a new transmission path from gold prices to credit quality.
insights.quote: Gold loans are now the second-largest retail lending segment after housing
insights.locator: Collateralised borrowing against gold jewellery

insights.claim: Loan-to-value ratios on Indian gold loans were reportedly around 55% for banks and 60% for NBFCs as of March 2026, with estimated collateral cover of around 1.5x on incremental gold loans at end-June 2026.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: 1.5x collateral cover means roughly a 33% gold price drawdown starts eroding the buffer — a quantifiable stress threshold for Indian gold-loan lenders.
insights.quote: our estimates indicate collateral cover of around 1.5x on incremental gold loans at end-June
insights.locator: Credit risks remain contained by relatively conservative loan-to-value ratios

insights.claim: A WGC-Kantar survey conducted between 22 May and 3 June 2026 covered 1,963 Indian consumers aged 18-65 across 12 metro and Tier I cities to test responses to record gold prices.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Primary-survey evidence collected at the price peak gives a forward read on Indian demand that lags official tonnage data by a quarter.
insights.locator: Consumers recalibrate gold purchase

insights.claim: The survey found Indian gold's role is broadening beyond traditional and occasion-led purchases towards financial security and investment, with purchase intent stronger for investment gold than for jewellery.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The demand mix is structurally rotating from jewellery to bars, coins, ETFs and digital gold — favour investment-product distributors over pure jewellery retail.
insights.quote: Purchase intent is stronger for investment gold than for jewellery
insights.locator: The key findings were

insights.claim: The WGC-Kantar survey found high prices have tempered discretionary Indian jewellery demand while wedding- and festival-related purchases appear relatively resilient, and exchange offers, savings schemes and EMIs are supporting demand.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The non-discretionary wedding/festive core is the hard floor under Indian demand; financing and exchange schemes are now the clearing mechanism for everything above it.
insights.quote: Exchange offers, savings schemes and EMIs are supporting demand
insights.locator: The key findings were

themes.theme: Outlook and downside risks for H2 2026

insights.claim: The World Gold Council expects Indian gold demand to remain sensitive to price movements, with both price stability and dips supporting purchases, and wedding- and festive-related buying providing seasonal support for the remainder of 2026.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Indian demand should act as a shock absorber on price dips into H2, cushioning corrections but not driving upside.
insights.quote: Indian gold demand is likely to remain sensitive to price movements, with both price stability and dips supporting purchases.
insights.locator: Outlook

insights.claim: The foremost downside risk to Indian gold demand is a weaker-than-normal monsoon, which could weigh on rural incomes and temper demand, alongside further domestic price rises or adverse policy measures.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Monsoon rainfall data is a tradeable leading indicator for Indian gold demand in H2 2026 — track IMD deviation alongside import duty announcements.
insights.quote: The foremost is a weaker-than-normal monsoon, which could weigh on rural incomes and temper demand.
insights.locator: There are, however, downside risks
